name: Alvin Chapman
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I got my first supervisor job after the preferred applicant turned up in the wrong city.” People around Tideline Market know Alvin by a small Monday habit. Alvin picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I hired him to meet customers. On day one he showed me how much you can learn from an unfinished sleeve.
appearance: Alvin has a blunt cut just below the ears, a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, and a favorite piece of clothing, a sand-colored linen shirt. It usually goes with a small enamel bird on the lapel. When somebody else has the floor, Alvin presses the lips together to keep a smile in.
personality: Alvin is cheerful on a bad morning and unexpectedly melancholy after a success. Finishing a hard thing means losing the daily company of the people who worked on it.
agenda: To give the new hire a front-counter shift with a fair wage.
family: Alejandro Sanders is Alvin’s half-sibling. Alvin makes the call. Alejandro is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *Spin cycle choir*, Alejandro says, “I have tuned pianos for years. This is the first chord I've been paid to leave out of tune.”
connections: Celia Baxter. The cupboard organizer finds an employer willing to let the new hire choose real work clothes. Also in the story is Quinn Pereira (new hire).

reactions.response: Alvin says what they know in their own name and refuses to treat a guess as something the child has to disprove.
